positions.as_written: Expect patellofemoral pathology to present on stairs, given the simultaneous rise in angle and quadriceps force.
Treat a timed stair test as a performance measure rather than a kinematic one.
Treat stair function as a discriminating outcome measure, since it needs more range and more eccentric control than the tasks most patients recover first.
Use stair function rather than level walking when judging whether a knee has recovered.
Consider mid flexion instability in a replaced knee whose only complaint is stairs.
Exclude quadriceps weakness before attributing stair difficulty to the mechanics.
